text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Thursday.

GERMANY - German Bunds and futures were lower in late dealings, hurt by ongoing fears of a delay in European currency union and growing prospects for a U.S. interest rate hike. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 99.77, down 0.18 from Wednesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts were dragged lower into the close by U.S. bonds which slid on comments by Fed chairman Alan Greenspan that he would set monetary policy pre-emptively. U.S. market now sees rate rise at March 25 meeting. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 109-01/32, down 09/32 from Wednesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures slipped amid caution ahead of a series of U.S. economic releases, a speech by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan and persistant concerns about European monetary union. The June notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 127.32, down 0.58 from Wednesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bond futures edged into positive territory in late afternoon despite comments by Fed chairman Alan Greenspan which fuelled speculation of a U.S. rate rise. The words depressed many bonds markets but BTPs gained in a technical recovery. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 125.45, up 0.58 from Wednesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasury prices were steady after sliding on view Fed will hike interest rates at policy makers meet on March 25. The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 108-11/32, down 04/32 from Wednesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 7.00 percent.
JAPAN - The Tokyo Japanese government bond and futures market is closed for a National Holiday, The market will reopen on Friday.

EUROBONDS - The primary market had its busiest session for some while as borrowers emerged in a plethora of currencies. Korea's Export-Import Bank issued an expected $500 million 10-year global bond with an investor put option after five years. The notes will be priced 50-53 basis points over the five-year U.S. Treasury note. Lehman Brothers was lead manager.
